newsitem.title: UK: Entergy says talks with London end.
newsitem.headline: Entergy says talks with London end.

text.p: U.S. energy group Entergy said on Wednesday that exploratory discussions with Britain's London Electricity Plc had taken place but "have now been discontinued."

Responding to recent newspaper speculation that the company might be considering a bid for the British regional electricity company, Entergy spokesman Patrick Sweeney said the company continued to consider the UK an attractive market.
"We continue to evaluate attractive markets and investment opportunities worldwide and consider the UK market to be in that category," Sweeney said in a statement.

London Electricity shares rose sharply on the stock market on Tuesday, closing up 30-1/2 pence at 667 pence, after a report in the Wall Street Journal Europe that Entergy was mulling a 1.2 billion pound bid which would be around 700 pence per share.
London Electricity had declined to comment on the report but Entergy had declined to rule it out, adding that any talks were at too early a stage to be "really meaningful".

Recs have seen a flurry of renewed bid fever in recent weeks as two of the last five remaining independent have attracted offers -- Northern Electric is fending off U.S.-based CalEnergy and East Midlands has agreed takeover by Dominion Resoures. ($1=.5970 Pound)
